status: direction proposed and adopted; colour + accessibility half enforced by a build gate (now including chart-series contrast and colour-blind distinguishability, closed 2026-08-30), signature elements specified but mostly NOT yet built (see implementation status on each)
why_this_file_exists: Greg has asked three times that BidlowAI systems stop looking generic. Nothing was ever written down, so every screen was a fresh decision and the answer drifted back to the framework default each time.

This file is the direction of record. It is not a mood board: the parts that can be machine-checked are machine-checked by src/lib/design/design-system.test.ts, which runs in the same gate as every other test and fails the build on drift.

An artefact nobody reads and nothing enforces is this project's single worst defect class (eight instances this week of 'built, wired, reports success, never fires'). A design document is an unusually easy ninth. So the colour tokens and the WCAG ratios here are read out of this file and asserted against the shipped stylesheet.

direction.name: Ledger & Rail
direction.thesis: An outreach console is a ledger of things that have left the building and cannot be recalled. It should read like a well-kept record, and everything capable of leaving the building should be visibly marked as such.

principles.statement: Consequence is drawn, not merely confirmed in a dialog.
principles.detail: The system reserves one visual idiom — the send rail — exclusively for surfaces representing mail that has left, or is about to leave, for a third party. Nothing decorative may use it. Irreversibility becomes legible at a glance rather than something you learn from a modal you have already stopped reading.
principles.why_here: This product's defining risk is that a defect reaches a stranger's inbox and cannot be recalled, and its worst recurring defect is a thing that looks live and is not. Both are answered by making 'this is real' a property of the chrome.

principles.detail: Density, alignment, tabular numerals and typographic hierarchy carry the structure. Boxes inside boxes, and drop shadows used to express hierarchy on in-flow surfaces, are banned. Staff live in this all day; a record rewards that, a dashboard does not.
principles.why_here: Discovery says the one screen staff live in is the client workspace and its activity inbox. Those are lists of events over time. That is a ledger, and it should be typeset as one.

principles.detail: The chrome is a low-chroma neutral carrying a faint green hue — chosen, not pure grey — so that the few genuinely coloured pixels on screen are always state: a bounce, a dead mailbox, a suppression, a claim. Colour is a scarce resource spent only on things that changed or need a decision.
principles.why_here: The generic admin template spends colour on decoration and then has nothing left to say when something is actually wrong.

direction.what_makes_it_not_generic: The default outcome — and what the app is closest to today — is shadcn's neutral palette with a brand hue swapped in. That is recognisably a template. The escape is not more decoration; it is one idiom the domain earns and no template ships: a reserved marker for irreversibility, applied with discipline and never anywhere else.

audience_and_conditions.primary_users: OpensDoors operations staff, at an office desk, on a laptop, in the product for most of a working day
audience_and_conditions.not_users: the email recipients — they never see this UI, only the mail it sends
audience_and_conditions.the_one_screen_they_live_in: client workspace → activity (the reply inbox). Optimise that; the rest may be plain.
audience_and_conditions.conditions: desktop-first, mouse and keyboard, good connection, dual monitors common. Mobile is a check-in surface (PWA installed), not a working surface.
audience_and_conditions.note: Recorded from what the build already assumes. Marked as an assumption, not observed fact — nobody has yet watched a member of staff work for an hour. That observation is ASK's outstanding discovery gap (queue item 8), and it may correct this block.

tokens.note: Authoritative source is src/app/globals.css. These values are asserted equal to it by design-system.test.ts, in both themes — if the two drift, the build fails and names the token.

hue_policy.rule: Neutrals sit two degrees off the brand hue at very low chroma (0.004–0.014). They are a chosen near-grey, not #888. This is the cheapest single thing that stops a palette reading as a template, and it is why --background is 0.004 chroma rather than 0.
hue_policy.forbidden_hues: No hue in the 260–320 band (the violet/indigo of the default framework theme). See anti-goals.

display.used_for: page titles (h1) and card titles only
display.rule: The display face is a signature, and a signature used everywhere is a texture. Never on body copy, never on table cells, never on buttons.

mono.used_for: message ids, addresses, template placeholders, anything a person will copy

numerals.rule: Every number that can change — a count, a total, a percentage, a duration — is set in tabular figures (`tabular-nums`).
numerals.why: Columns align, and a count that ticks from 9 to 10 does not shove the row sideways. In a ledger this is not a nicety.

radius.rule: One radius scale, derived from one base. Nothing is fully rounded except avatars.

elevation.rule: Shadow means 'this floats above the page', and is permitted ONLY on genuinely floating layers: popover, dropdown, select menu, sheet, tooltip, dialog.
elevation.banned: Shadow as a hierarchy device on in-flow surfaces. Cards separate from the canvas by a hairline plus a ground-tone shift (--card is lighter than --background), never by a shadow.
elevation.known_exception: src/components/ui/card.tsx currently carries shadow-xs and tabs.tsx carries shadow-sm. Both are inherited from the shadcn defaults, both are in-flow, and both are therefore out of line with this rule. Left in place this cycle — removing them is a visual change across every screen and belongs with the UI consolidation (queue item 7), not with the artefact that names the rule.

motion.rule: Motion confirms a state change and nothing else. No entrance animation on page content, no parallax, no attention-seeking loops.
motion.duration: 150–200ms for state, up to 300ms for a layer entering
motion.reduced_motion: Must honour prefers-reduced-motion; anything that moves more than an opacity fade needs a reduced variant.

signature_elements.name: The send rail
signature_elements.what: A 3px hard left edge on any surface that represents mail which has left, or is about to leave, for a third party — a queued row, a sent message, a launch panel, a sequence step. Colour encodes where it is on the one-way trip: queued (muted), sent (primary), delivered (primary), bounced (destructive), suppressed (muted with a struck pattern).
signature_elements.rule: RESERVED. A left-edge rule of this weight may appear nowhere else in the product for any decorative reason. Its meaning is the whole value; spend it and it is gone.
signature_elements.why_it_is_ours: It is drawn from what this product actually is. No admin template ships a marker for irreversibility, because no admin template knows which of its rows can reach a stranger.
signature_elements.implementation_status: NOT BUILT. Specified here. No border-l of any weight currently exists in the codebase outside a scroll-area internal, so the idiom is unclaimed and free to take.

signature_elements.name: Live and dry banding
signature_elements.what: Any surface where an action will really send carries the outbound tint and says so in words. Simulated, internal-seed, dev-route and dry-run surfaces carry a neutral hatched ground.
signature_elements.rule: The distinction is never carried by a word alone in body copy. It is a property of the surface, visible before anything is read.
signature_elements.why_it_is_ours: This project has shipped eight things this week that looked live and were not. The interface should make the difference impossible to misread, in both directions.
signature_elements.implementation_status: NOT BUILT. Partially anticipated by the existing governed-send-display helper, which already computes whether a send is real.

signature_elements.name: Tabular numerals everywhere a count appears
signature_elements.implementation_status: PARTIAL — 45 usages already in the codebase. Not yet universal and not yet enforced.
signature_elements.build_with: opportunistically; a lint rule is not worth writing yet

signature_elements.name: The display face, rationed
signature_elements.what: Bricolage Grotesque on h1 and card titles; Geist everywhere else.
signature_elements.implementation_status: BUILT — globals.css applies font-heading to h1, and card titles inherit it.

signature_elements.name: State carries a word, a shape and a colour — never colour alone
signature_elements.what: Every status is a label plus an icon or shape, with colour as reinforcement. A red dot on its own is not a status.
signature_elements.rule: Required by WCAG 1.4.1, but it is also just correct for a ledger someone scans quickly.
signature_elements.implementation_status: MOSTLY BUILT — the badge component and the mailbox connection states already pair word with colour. Not audited screen by screen; that audit is owed.

signature_elements.name: Hairline and ground
signature_elements.what: Surfaces separate by a 1px hairline plus a shift in ground tone, not by a shadow.
signature_elements.implementation_status: MOSTLY BUILT — --card is deliberately lighter than --background in light mode and lighter again in dark. Undermined by the inherited shadow-xs on cards; see tokens.elevation.known_exception.

anti_goals.rule: No violet or indigo accent — no hue in the 260–320 band. That palette is the default framework theme and reads instantly as an unfinished template.
No gradient hero panels, no glassmorphism, no blur-behind surfaces. This is an operations console, not a landing page.

No emoji used as a status indicator or icon. They render differently on every platform, they are read aloud unpredictably by screen readers, and they make a production console look like a hobby project.
No drop shadow on in-flow surfaces. Shadow means floating. See tokens.elevation.
Colour is never the sole carrier of meaning. WCAG 1.4.1.
Three families total — display, body, mono. A fourth is a decision to be argued for, not made in passing.
No full-bleed centred marketing layout inside the application. Content is left-aligned and works to the width of the window.
No icon-only control without an accessible name.

Foreground is never pure black and the canvas is never pure white. --foreground is 0.24 lightness and --background is 0.975 with a trace of hue. Maximum contrast is not maximum readability, and pure #000 on #fff is the visual signature of nobody having chosen anything.
The send rail is never decorative. See signature_elements.send-rail.

accessibility.why_this_standard: The UK Equality Act applies to private-sector services, and OpensDoors' own prospects include public-sector bodies whose procurement asks the question. WCAG 2.2 is the current W3C Recommendation; 2.1 is the older one and quoting it in 2026 would be quoting a superseded standard.

accessibility.honest_scope: Four of these are machine-gated on every build. The rest are recorded commitments checked by hand, and most have not yet been checked. This file does not claim the product is WCAG 2.2 AA conformant. It claims the colour system is, and names precisely what is still owed.

known_judgement_call.decision: Not treated as a 1.4.11 failure and deliberately not changed.
known_judgement_call.reasoning: 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for visual information required to IDENTIFY a component or its state. A card edge, a table rule and a divider are decorative — remove them entirely and every component is still identifiable. Darkening every hairline in the product to satisfy a rule that does not apply to them would wreck the calm-chrome principle for no accessibility gain.
known_judgement_call.where_it_does_apply: --input, which is the sole identifier of a text field, a textarea and a select trigger — all three are bg-transparent, so with a faint border there is nothing on screen to say a control is there at all. That is a genuine failure and it is gated.
known_judgement_call.reviewable: If a future reviewer disagrees, the pair is one line in contrast_pairs with role ui_component and the gate will enforce it.

contrast_pairs.note: link and inline-primary text on the canvas
destructive button label — the variant is a tint, so the label sits on near-canvas
the boundary of a text field, and its only identifier
chart series contrast — WCAG 1.4.11, non-text meaningful graphic

decisions_taken_this_cycle.decision: Adopt 'Ledger & Rail' as the direction without asking Greg first.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.why: The queue item says to propose a direction and not wait to be told one. The direction is derived from what the product does rather than from taste, so it is arguable on evidence rather than on preference.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.reversible: Yes, cheaply. Nothing built depends on the name; the two unbuilt signature elements are the only commitments it makes.

decisions_taken_this_cycle.decision: Fix the --input contrast failure by changing the token value, rather than by introducing a separate --input-border token.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.why: border-input has 34 call sites across 15 files — hand-rolled inputs, not just the ui/ primitives. Changing the token is one line and fixes all 34. A new token would be a 15-file diff touching most forms in the product, which is a UI-consolidation-sized change and does not belong in the cycle that writes the design artefact.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.cost: --input is also used as a low-opacity fill in 12 places (bg-input/30, /50, /80 — dark-mode field grounds and disabled states). Those fills change: dark fields lift slightly, and disabled fields in light mode now read as clearly grey rather than near-white. Both are improvements, but they are visible and Greg should know they were not accidents.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.better_long_term: Split --input into --input (fill) and --input-border (boundary). They have different contrast requirements and conflating them is exactly why this failed. Recommended for queue item 7.

decisions_taken_this_cycle.why: At 0.577 it measured 4.44:1 against the canvas, against a required 4.5 for text — a second genuine pre-existing failure the gate found. 0.55 gives 4.80:1 on the canvas and 5.15:1 on a card. The hue and chroma are untouched, so the red is the same red, very slightly deeper.

decisions_taken_this_cycle.decision: (2026-08-26, cycle 9) Do not change the chart tokens, and do not gate chart contrast, despite having measured two failures.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.why: Darkening --chart-4 to reach 3:1 moves it to roughly 0.62 lightness at hue 162 — which puts it within 0.07 lightness of --chart-1 at the same hue, so the two series become hard to tell apart. Fixing the contrast properly means reconsidering categorical distinguishability across the whole series set at the same time, including for colour-blind readers. That is a real piece of design work, not a token nudge, and doing it hastily at the end of this cycle would trade a measurable defect for an unmeasured one.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.recorded_as: open_defects.chart-series-contrast at the time; superseded by the 2026-08-30 entry below, which closes it

decisions_taken_this_cycle.decision: (2026-08-30, cycle 133) Replace all four chart tokens with a freshly-derived, computed palette; drop --chart-5 rather than ship it broken. Closes open_defects.chart-series-contrast.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.why: The prior chart-3/chart-4 pairing measured 2.51:1 and 2.39:1 against the card in light mode (below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 floor), and chart-1/chart-4 shared hue 162 — the cycle-9 finding above. A full re-derivation, computed and asserted by src/lib/design/chart-palette.test.ts (not eyeballed), grid-searched hue x lightness x chroma jointly for a set clearing all four bars this row set at once: >=3:1 contrast against --card in both themes; >=8.0 OKLab ΔE (x100) between every PAIR of series (not just neighbours — this project treats its chart tokens as usable in any combination, so it holds itself to the dataviz skill's stricter 'scatter/small-multiples' all-pairs check rather than the default adjacent-only one) under simulated protanopia and deuteranopia (Machado-Oliveira-Fernandes 2009, severity 1.0); >=15.0 ΔE under normal, unsimulated vision (the skill's hard floor); and no chart hue within 25 degrees of --destructive's hue (~27deg), so a chart series can never read as an error state. --chart-1 was held fixed at the brand hue (162, matching --primary) throughout the search so the result stays recognisably OpensDoors' green rather than a generic default.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.measured: Full before/after ratio and CVD-delta tables in docs/ops/CHART-SERIES-CONTRAST-2026-08-30.md. Final set clears every bar with margin in both themes (worst all-pairs CVD ΔE 10.6-10.9, worst normal-vision ΔE 20.0-21.1, worst contrast 3.80:1 light / 3.87:1 dark, tritan also checked and comfortably clears the same floor at 13.4-14.2 though the skill only formally gates protan/deutan). --chart-2's hue was set to 58, not the search's initial 52, after the chart-palette.test.ts destructive-collision check caught a 24.7deg gap against --destructive's light-mode hue (27.325) — a hair under the 25deg buffer the test requires; 58deg widens the gap to 30.7deg with no other bar affected.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.chart_5_dropped: An exhaustive search (same artefact) could not find a 5th hue, anchored on brand green at hue 162, that clears the all-pairs normal-vision floor together with the other four — best found was 14.2 ΔE against a required 15.0, a real measured near-miss, not a shortcut. Rather than ship a 5th token documented as failing a hard bar, --chart-5 and its @theme mapping were removed. If a 5th simultaneous series is ever genuinely needed: dropping the exact-162 brand anchor clears comfortably (an unconstrained 5-hue search reached ~10 CVD / ~18 normal-vision ΔE), or a constrained 5th slot can ship with mandatory secondary encoding (dash pattern, marker shape, or direct label) rather than relying on hue alone.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.reversible: Yes — the token values and the proven-safe count are both named constants (globals.css, DESIGN.json, and PROVEN_SAFE_CHART_TOKEN_COUNT in chart-palette.test.ts); revisiting the cap is a value change in three places, not an architecture change.

decisions_taken_this_cycle.why: See accessibility.known_judgement_call. Applying 1.4.11 to decorative hairlines is a misreading of the criterion and would cost the calm-chrome principle for no gain.

decisions_taken_this_cycle.decision: Leave the inherited shadow-xs on cards and shadow-sm on tabs in place, while writing the rule that forbids them.
decisions_taken_this_cycle.why: Removing them changes every screen. Naming the rule and the exception in the same file is honest; quietly shipping the visual change inside a documentation cycle is not.

enforcement.runs_in: npm test — the same gate as everything else, so it blocks CI and therefore merge
what_it_asserts: every colour token named in tokens.colour exists in src/app/globals.css with exactly that value, in both :root and .dark
no token in globals.css is missing from this file (drift in either direction fails)
every pair in contrast_pairs meets its min_ratio in both themes, computed from the real oklch values through the full sRGB conversion
the machine_checked anti-goals hold: no hue in the forbidden violet band, no pure black on pure white
every button size variant is at least 24px in both dimensions (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8)

chart-palette.test.ts: every chart token is >=3:1 against --card in both themes; every PAIR of chart tokens (not just neighbours) clears an OKLab ΔE >= 8.0 under simulated protanopia and deuteranopia, and >= 15.0 under normal vision (hard gate), and >= 6.0 under simulated tritanopia (regression guard); no chart hue sits within 25deg of --destructive's hue; the chart token count matches the number proven safe by the last search
enforcement.proven_to_fire: Yes, on real ground, twice. First on --input (1.21:1 against the light canvas, 1.30:1 against a card, against a required 3:1). Second on the chart palette (2026-08-30): chart-palette.test.ts was written and run against the UNCHANGED tokens before any fix, and failed red — --chart-4 at 2.39:1 against a required 3:1, and --chart-1 vs --chart-2 at 7.6 ΔE against a required 8.0/15.0 under CVD and normal vision respectively. Neither was a manufactured red.
enforcement.not_enforced: Everything in anti_goals with machine_checked false, and every accessibility commitment marked 'by hand'. Those are honest commitments, not gates. Do not read this file as a conformance claim.

open_defects.what: The destructive button variant is `bg-destructive/10 text-destructive`, so its label sits on a tint of its own colour rather than on the plain canvas. Measured against the real composite: 3.72:1 at rest and 3.31:1 on hover, against a required 4.5. Darkening --destructive to 0.55 lifts these to 4.01 and 3.56 — better, still failing.
open_defects.why_not_fixed_here: Reaching 4.5 on the hover state by token alone needs roughly 0.46 lightness, which is a visibly different, much deeper red across the whole product. The real fix is to the variant — a solid destructive ground with a light label, which is what the primary button already does — and that is a component change, not a token change.
open_defects.severity: AA text failure on a control that deletes things. Should be fixed.

open_defects.what: card.tsx carries shadow-xs and tabs.tsx carries shadow-sm — both in-flow, both against the elevation rule this file sets.
open_defects.why_not_fixed_here: Visual change on every screen; belongs with the consolidation.

open_questions_for_greg: Nobody has watched a member of OpensDoors staff work in this product for an hour. The audience_and_conditions block is inferred from the code, not observed. That observation would confirm or correct the claim that the activity inbox is the screen that matters most — and it is the same gap ASK has open as queue item 8.

The two real signature elements — the send rail and live/dry banding — are specified and not built. They are the whole of what stops this looking like a template, and they need queue item 7 (UI consolidation, PR #196) to land first, because that PR moves the surfaces they would attach to.
